content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors introduce a new test-set to measure progress on object-recognition performances. The paper is another work in the direction of works such as ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-C and ObjectNet to identify test benchmarks other than the standard ImageNet validation set. According to the authors, existing benchmarks either closely follow ImageNet in terms of protocols (ImageNet-V2), focus on worst-case performance (ImageNet-A) or environment biases such as ObjectNet.

The D2O test-set consists of 8K images across 36 categories, 29 classes in common with ImageNet. The test-set also has a “miscellaneous” category which is essentially multilabel. They test ImageNet-pretrained models and vision API's on their dataset and notice a performance drop in accuracy.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strengths:**

The paper is generally easy to read and the authors tackle an interesting problem. The authors also incorporate recent image-to-text generative models which is novel.

**Weaknesses:**

--------

**ImageNet-R comparisons** :
The paper should position itself in context with ImageNet-R. The ImageNet-R paper specifically "contains various artistic renditions of object classes from the original ImageNet dataset". They also evaluate ImageNet models on several out-of-distribution datasets, which seem to have some level of overlap with the D2O dataset. For example, Figure 2 of the ImageNet-R paper, shows renditions of ImageNet images with paintings and sculptures, which seem to be similar to the dataset presented in the paper.

**Insights on ImageNet modeling**:

The insights or takeaway messages seem to be somewhat similar to the other ImageNet-"X" papers discussed in the introduction. That is, even though there is a steady drop in these out-of-the-distribution datasets, better performance on ImageNet seems to correlate with better performace OOD. It is unclear to me what differentiates this paper from other such works in terms of empirical insights.

***Actionable Feedback:*** The authors should add discussion on what differentiates their paper from the ImageNet-R dataset. Also, the authors could add discussions on what additional insights this paper can offer as compared to the previous ImageNet-X works.

-----------------

**Dataset Collection**: The information about the dataset collection procedure lacks in details as compared to related works (for eg, See: Section 4 of ImageNet-V2). It is also disappointing that researchers have to fill up a form to get permission to evaluate models on the D2O dataset, when standard benchmarks are open-souce and available readily on TFDS.

**Clarity** : The paper can improve on clarity in a number of places.

***Actionable Feedback***: See below for detailed comments. Please incorporate these in the next revision.

---------------

[1] The Many Faces of Robustness: A Critical Analysis of Out-of-Distribution Generalization ICCV 2021
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
**Clarity and Quality**

----
**Dataset Quality**

The major contribution of paper seems to be the dataset itself but it lacks several details:

* Page 4: "We only selected the images that had good quality": How is image quality ensured, precisely? What mechanism was used to filter down the initially queried/generated images to the final test-set?
* Page 4: We did our best to ensure that images do contain sensitive material, have poor resolution, or violate copyright law": How was it ensure that there was no sensitive material and by what definition?
* Page 4: During data collection, we emphasized choosing the odd items: What does this mean?
* Page 4: Most of the images contain one main object. How is this ensured?
* Page 4: images from various categorized panels : What does this mean?
* Why is the class frequency in Figure 2 arbitrary? What is the design decision behing not having a fixed number of high quality samples per category?

**Miscellaneous**

* Page 4: How many samples were used to compute the FID?
* Fig 5: Legends are unclear. Are the dashed lines: average ImageNet-top1 and ImageNet-top5. Why do they have different colors than the other bars?
* Fig 5: The models in the caption and title are different.
* Fig 6: Since the training set of the WSL model is different from the others, it makes sense to represent this as a point.
* Fig 7: What are the ground truths for the bottom two rows in Figure 7?
* Section 4.1: "The best Top-1 and Top-5 performance over the latter are about 91% and 99%, respectively". This is true, but I belive the models that achieve those are not considered in Fig 6.

**Section 4.2**

* General: How is the tagging API different from general multilabel classification?
* Face detection: It is mentioned that IOU >= 0.5 is a true positive. How is the ground truth bounding box generated?
* What is the label space off the API's described? Do they contain all the ground truth labels from the D2O dataset?
* Have the authors evaluated the vision API's on ImageNet? Do they correlate with the D2O dataset?


**Novelty and Reproducibilty:** See strengths and weaknesses.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The authors introduce a new dataset to evaluate ImageNet (and related) object classification benchmarks.

I think some work is needed to position this work in terms of related work (ImageNet-R) and new insights. I left some feedback regarding the clarity of the paper. The dataset also requires a form to be signed to be used, which hinders its adoption.

One novel aspect of the paper is the usage of text-to-image models for evalation. I encourage the authors to push their work more in this direction, as it might lead to some new insights.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a new test set for object classification, which contains diverse and hard examples for current image classification models trained on ImageNet. The accuracy of SoTA models are shown to drop significantly (91% -> 60%) on this new test set. They also test cloud APIs of big companies, and find they sometimes perform poorly on these hard images. They believe this test set can challenge object recognition for years to come.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength

1. This work certainly highlights an important problem of existing object recognition research. We are overly focused on a handful of benchmark datasets such as ImageNet, overlooking generalization to more diverse, hard and odd images. Existing test sets might not faithfully reflect what models need to deal with in the real world.

2. The proposed D2O dataset appears to be a good additional test set for model evaluation. It covers sufficient diversity and hard cases to mitigate the problem mentioned above.

3. I especially like the part about synthesizing test images with SoTA generative models such as Dall-E 2, MidJourney and Stable Diffusion. As generated pictures popularize, it is important to understand how models would react to them.

Weakness

1. Testing only ImageNet pre-trained models is not enough. I think the problem pointed out in this paper is probably mainly due to data rather than algorithm, i.e., the bias of the ImageNet-1K training set itself, and domain gap. What about models pre-trained on other datasets, e.g., ImageNet-22K, CLIP? Is the problem still there? If it’s mainly a data problem, shall we try to fix the training set?

2. Similarly, I think it can be interesting to test models pre-trained with other algorithms, such as contrastive learning, autoencoding, on the ImageNet-1K. This is to see whether the problem is due to the training algorithm.

3. I feel the new test set does not add many new insights. We already know that ImageNet has limitations: biased towards object-centric images, biased coverage of categories, incorrect labels, unable to handle cluttered scenes due to single class prediction, etc. What are the additional discoveries made in this paper? Could authors clarify their new insights/contributions? And maybe give some hints on how researchers can benefit from the new test set?

Other minor comments: 

- Some test images are maybe too hard or inappropriate. For example, Fig.7 the first row, the 5th image, I think it's probably fine to predict "knot" instead of "kite" as it's actually a knot; also "hen", "apron" seem right?
- It would be interesting to consider real images and synthetic images separately, as they might have systematic distribution differences.
- (Typos) Figure 2 caption, missing ‘.’ at the end. Figure 5 caption, missing ‘)’. Sec 5 ending, missing space in Appendix H.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The quality and clarity of presentation are good. They include many charts and examples to illustrate their points. The originality is ok, but see weakness in novelty in previous section.
content.summary_of_the_review:
I think this paper emphasizes an important problem—the shortcomings of existing classification benchmarks, and provides a new test dataset to address it.

However, I feel the discovery is somewhat not new, or not much different from what we already know (Recht et al., Hendrycks et al., Barbu et al.). I hope the authors can give us more insights on how they are different and how to use their test set to foster future research.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a dataset (D2O) for object recognition. Unlike common datasets, D2O consists of only the test set and no training set. The goal is to evaluate the performance on this test set while training can be done on any set.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

1. D2O is an interesting dataset that is manually verified and annotated. The license issues for the images are taken care of. 

2. D2O consists of unusual classes beyond Imagenet. 

3. Authors conducted experiments with a range of state-of-the-art models to benchmark the performance of this set.

Weaknesses:

1. Authors claim that the dataset is diverse and difficult and didn't justify this claim. How is the diversity estimated? The low accuracy on this set doesn't justify the difficulty as the performance also depends on the training set and training/adaptation approach. 

2. The dataset (8060 images with 36 categories) is not large with respect to the current standards. 

3. The dataset consists of synthetic images that can appear different from natural images. What is the motivation to combine both while evaluating an approach?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The draft the clearly written and easy to follow. The dataset, if released, can be reused.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors collect a new test set for image classification. Compared with the previous evaluation sets, the new dataset alleviates the shortcomings of the existing evolution sets like bias on ImageNet characteristics, and it is more diverse and representative of real-world images. The authors also conduct extensive experiments to study the property of the new evaluation set.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1.	A more diverse and practical evaluation dataset / metric is of great importance to help us better understand the performance, robustness, and generalization of the machine learning models. The new evaluation set could set a new standard for evaluating object detection.
2.	The method to collect the new dataset is interesting as the authors explore some search-based methods as well as strong generative models like Dall-E 2.
3.	Sufficient experiment results demonstrate that the current object recognition models cannot get great results on the new set as they do on the ImageNet test set, suggesting that the new set could help us better understand the current image classification models.

Weakness:
1.	It would make this paper stronger if the authors can show some adversarial robustness of some SOTA defended recognition models on the new set.
2.	I would like to see more clear details of how to use DALL-E2 or stable diffusion models to generate hard examples, e.g., how to design prompts and how to filter out some unrealistic images.
3.	The new dataset has some great properties. However, how to make it more scalable to real applications besides evaluating the current models trained on a public dataset? What if we have some new classes in our task, but it is not included in this set?
4.	It is still unclear how to make the new proposed evaluation set more diverse and representative than the previous method and how to select those representative images.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well-organized and easy to follow.
